changelog: **USB hub support — mouse *and* keyboard at once (AIM).** A hub on the host port was previously dead; the device saw nothing behind it. Now a mouse and a keyboard on the same hub work together: the mouse aims, the keyboard drives controller buttons. This was physically impossible before — the firmware could only ever claim one of the two.

**Keyboard → left stick (movement).** WASD (configurable) now drives the **left** analog stick, where every game expects movement. Diagonals are normalised so diagonal isn't faster than straight. The left stick was previously hard-wired to neutral, so there was nowhere for movement to go — WASD sat on the D-pad, which no game uses to walk.

**Mouse buttons and wheel are now freely assignable.** In the AIM button assignment, each controller button can take a keyboard key **or** a mouse button/wheel as its trigger — pick it in the same "Set" capture. Previously the mouse buttons were hard-wired (Left→A, Right→B, …) and could not be changed.

**MKCOMBO — mouse + keyboard combined (Firmware A).** With a hub, Firmware A now runs the mouse (MIM cursor correction) and the keyboard (KIM sequences) at the same time. This mode existed in name only before and silently behaved like plain MIM.

**New AIM default binding.** WASD on the left stick; the five mouse buttons on A/B/X/Y/R3; Shift/Space on the analog triggers LT/RT; D-pad on 1/2/3/4; L3 on Left-Ctrl. AIM settings are reset once to these defaults on update (MIM/CIM/KIM profiles are untouched — separate profiles, separate addresses). Mouse wheel up/down are now assignable but unbound by default (were fixed to RB/View).

**MIM stayed safe with a hub attached.** Keyboard modifiers (Shift/Ctrl/Alt/GUI) are no longer passed through to the PC in MIM/AIM mode when a hub enumerates a keyboard — without the gate, MIM would have leaked modifiers while swallowing normal keys, i.e. a half-dead keyboard. Verified on hardware: the device sees the Shift, the PC does not.

**Firmware version reported itself as 2.8.0.** The version string was not pulled during releases, so a device on 2.9.0 answered "2.8.0" — a bug report would have chased the wrong version. Now bumped and read back after flashing.
